data.title: A word beside the photograph

memoryNodes.cue: Lin keeps a question beside the photograph caption.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 林在照片图注旁保留一个问题。

memoryNodes.cue: The tutor asks them to adapt a short story.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 导师请她们改编一篇短篇故事。

memoryNodes.cue: Maya checks whether one word can replace another.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 玛雅核对一个词能否换成另一个。

data.situation:
On Monday, 6 September 2027, at ten past two, Lin was back at the library window table. The two market photographs were still in her notebook. Beside them lay an assignment card from the tutor: choose a short story and adapt part of it for a small performance. Lin wanted to build her vocabulary before choosing a book, but Maya pointed to the caption she had already written. The phrase “give way to” described the old stalls disappearing as new shops opened. One line needed a small change in grammar: “Old stalls give way to new shops”, not “Old stalls gives way to new shops”. Lin crossed out the extra letter. Instead of starting another long list, she put a question mark beside the sentence and opened the dictionary. Maya: Is “tiny” a synonym for “small” here?
Lin: For a stall, perhaps. But “a tiny business” might suggest something different.
Maya: Then keep the original sentence. What is an antonym for “empty”?
Lin: “Full”. This photograph shows a full square, while the other one shows it empty.
Maya: Write that beside the pictures. We can listen to your description next. Note from your tutor, beside the assignment card
The phrase “give way to” can describe the change from old stalls to new shops, but it does not explain why the change occurred. A caption such as “The stalls disappeared because rents rose” would present one possible explanation as a fact. The photographs, by themselves, provide no evidence of a rent increase. You can describe what you see while leaving the cause open: “The stalls may have disappeared for several reasons; we would need other records to investigate them.” Keep that distinction in the description you record next.

readingBlocks.en: On Monday, 6 September 2027, at ten past two, Lin was back at the library window table. The two market photographs were still in her notebook. Beside them lay an assignment card from the tutor: choose a short story and adapt part of it for a small performance. Lin wanted to build her vocabulary before choosing a book, but Maya pointed to the caption she had already written. The phrase “give way to” described the old stalls disappearing as new shops opened. One line needed a small change in grammar: “Old stalls give way to new shops”, not “Old stalls gives way to new shops”. Lin crossed out the extra letter. Instead of starting another long list, she put a question mark beside the sentence and opened the dictionary.
readingBlocks.zh: 2027年9月6日星期一，下午两点十分，林又坐到了图书馆窗边的桌旁。两张集市照片仍夹在笔记本里，旁边放着导师的作业卡：选一篇短篇故事，把其中一部分改编成小小的演出。林想先积累词汇再选书，玛雅却指了指她已经写好的图注。“give way to”这个词组，描述了旧摊位逐渐消失、新商店开起来的变化。有一行的语法需要稍作调整：应写“Old stalls give way to new shops”，而不是“Old stalls gives way to new shops”。林划掉了多出的字母。她没有再开一张长词表，而是在句旁打了个问号，翻开词典。

readingBlocks.en:
Maya: Is “tiny” a synonym for “small” here?
Lin: For a stall, perhaps. But “a tiny business” might suggest something different.
Maya: Then keep the original sentence. What is an antonym for “empty”?
Lin: “Full”. This photograph shows a full square, while the other one shows it empty.
Maya: Write that beside the pictures. We can listen to your description next.
readingBlocks.zh:
玛雅：这里的“tiny”能作为“small”的近义词吗？
林：形容摊位或许可以，但“a tiny business”可能会让人想到别的意思。
玛雅：那就先保留原句。“empty”的反义词是什么？
林：“full”。这张照片里的广场满是人，另一张里却空着。
玛雅：把这点写在照片旁边。接下来我们可以听听你怎样描述。

readingBlocks.en:
Note from your tutor, beside the assignment card
The phrase “give way to” can describe the change from old stalls to new shops, but it does not explain why the change occurred. A caption such as “The stalls disappeared because rents rose” would present one possible explanation as a fact. The photographs, by themselves, provide no evidence of a rent increase. You can describe what you see while leaving the cause open: “The stalls may have disappeared for several reasons; we would need other records to investigate them.” Keep that distinction in the description you record next.
readingBlocks.zh:
导师留在作业卡旁的便条
“give way to”这个词组可以描述旧摊位被新商店取代的变化，却没有解释变化为什么发生。“摊位消失是因为租金上涨”这样的图注，会把一种可能的解释写成事实。仅凭照片，并没有租金上涨的证据。你可以描述所见，同时不急着确定原因：“摊位消失可能有多种原因；我们需要其他记录来进一步调查。”接下来录制描述时，也要区分所见的变化和可能的解释。

glossary.note: 这里名词grammar指组织词句的规则；完整图注中的stalls为复数，动词要求give，不选gives。引号内错误版本作为已改错误展示。

retrievalPrompts.cue: You know some words but are unsure how to put them into a sentence. Tell a classmate what you need.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 向同学说明你现在遇到的语言问题：知道几个词，却不确定怎么放进句子。
acceptableAnswers: I want to build my vocabulary, but I also need help with the grammar of this phrase.
checks: 表达与眼前情境相符；允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: A friend wants to replace small with tiny in your caption. Explain why you still need to check the sentence.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 朋友想把图注里的small换成tiny，你会怎样说明为什么还得看整句？
acceptableAnswers: Tiny is a synonym for small, but I need to check whether it fits this sentence.
checks: 表达与眼前情境相符；允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: One photograph shows an empty square; the other is crowded. Describe them using words with opposite meanings.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 你拿着一张空广场照片和一张挤满人的照片，请用一对意思相反的词描述。
acceptableAnswers: Empty and full are antonyms here: one square is empty and the other is full.
checks: 表达与眼前情境相符；允许其他自然说法
